clue.text: Priest altered position in campaign

indicators.note: altered says the letters of the word priest are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A clergyman has been moved to a different post during some campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'altered' turns PRIEST into SITREP. A sitrep is military shorthand for a situation report.
explanation.definitionFit: A sitrep, short for situation report, tells commanders the current state of affairs during a military operation.

clue.text: Island's northerly capital importing trade

indicators.note: importing says one piece takes the other inside it
in a down clue, going northerly means the letters are read from the bottom up

parts.note: A1 means first-rate or capital, written AI in crosswords
biz is informal shorthand for business or trade

explanation.surface: An island's capital in the north brings in commerce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' is A1 (first-rate), written AI; 'northerly' reads it upwards in this down clue, giving IA, which 'importing' wraps round the trade word.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibiza is one of the Balearic Islands in the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Contrite man with fur let off

parts.note: Reg is a man's name, short for Reginald

indicators.note: off says the letters of fur and let go wrong and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man in a fur coat has been let off and feels sorry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' shuffles the letters of 'fur let'; the surface pictures someone in fur being let off, but 'off' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone contrite feels sorrow and remorse for what they have done.

clue.text: Parking by worthless hole

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
light can mean trivial or of little worth

explanation.surface: A car park next to a useless pit.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a hole means being in a predicament or difficult situation.

clue.text: Wine and beer around college? It provides good feeling

parts.note: tent is a deep red Spanish wine

indicators.note: around says the beer surrounds the college letter

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: Drinks around a university campus give everyone a warm glow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts C inside ALE. 'Good feeling' is cryptic: an octopus's arm is good at touching.
explanation.definitionFit: An octopus or squid uses its arms to touch and grope, so they are organs of touch.

clue.text: Drunk in loo beginning to surrender control and give up

indicators.note: in says the drunk is placed inside the loo

parts.note: throne is a jokey word for a lavatory
a wino is a drunkard

indicators.note: beginning to takes only the opening letter of surrender

parts.note: to have a hand in something is to have control of it

explanation.surface: A drunk in the toilet starts to concede and hands over control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Throne' is a jokey British word for a toilet; 'in' sets the drunk inside it, making THROWINONE, and 'beginning to' takes S from surrender.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom comes from cards: laying down your cards means you abandon the game, so you quit.

clue.text: Company in train sadly cold and inducing sleep

indicators.note: in says the company abbreviation sits inside the jumbled train letters
sadly signals that the letters of train are messed up

parts.note: C is the tap abbreviation for cold

explanation.surface: A firm on a train is miserable, chilly and sleepy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' signals the anagram of train, and 'in' sets the company abbreviation in the middle of the jumbled letters; the surface's gloomy train journey is misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: A narcotic drug dulls the senses and brings on drowsiness or stupor.

clue.text: A couple of bishops overlooking holy books for religious leader

indicators.note: in a down clue, overlooking means the bishops are placed above the holy books

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop, and a couple gives two of them
OT is the Old Testament, a collection of holy books

explanation.surface: Two bishops looking down on scripture, as a church leader might.
explanation.definitionFit: An abbot heads a community of monks in an abbey.

clue.text: Brief toss of a coin — call!

indicators.note: a toss throws things in the air, so the letters of a coin and call land in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone flips a coin and briskly says heads or tails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'toss of' rearranges A COIN and CALL. The calling of heads or tails is itself curt, fitting the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Laconical is a rarer form of laconic, describing speech that uses very few words.

clue.text: Reflective type that sticks out on estate?

definitions.text: Reflective type that sticks out on estate?

parts.words: Reflective type that sticks out on estate?
parts.note: reads like a thoughtful person standing out on a housing estate, but means a mirror projecting from the side of an estate car

explanation.definitionFit: It is the side mirror mounted outside a car door that a driver uses to see behind.

clue.text: Resist lively young man

explanation.surface: Fight back, energetic young chap.
explanation.definitionFit: To buck a trend is to oppose it; a buck is also an old word for a dashing young fellow.

clue.text: Some wag possibly inspiring hot TV programme

indicators.note: inspiring means breathing in, so the jumbled letters take another letter inside
possibly says the letters of some wag might be arranged differently

parts.note: H is the tap abbreviation for hot

explanation.surface: A joker might inspire a sizzling television show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' turns SOME WAG into GAMESOW; 'inspiring' puts H inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A quiz or panel format where contestants compete for prizes is a staple of television entertainment.

clue.text: Recommending timeless trip

indicators.note: timeless says the letter T, for time, is removed

parts.note: touting is pushing or promoting something

explanation.surface: Promoting a trip that will never date.
explanation.definitionFit: An outing is a short excursion or day out.

clue.text: Principal disheartened fellow devising courses

indicators.note: disheartened says the heart, the middle letter, is removed

parts.note: chief means principal or main

explanation.surface: The head man, depressed, plans a menu.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' takes the middle I out of CHIEF. The courses are meal courses, not classes.
explanation.definitionFit: A cook in a restaurant plans the dishes served as starters, mains and desserts.

clue.text: Slim-waisted girl supporting greedy chap around old city

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means the girl sits beneath the rest
around says the greedy chap goes round the old city

parts.note: a hog is a greedy person
Ur is the ancient city of Mesopotamia, a crossword stalwart
lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A slim girl props up a greedy man touring an ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: Ur, the ancient Mesopotamian city, goes into the greedy chap ('around') to make HOURG; 'supporting' in a down clue puts the girl underneath.
explanation.definitionFit: An hourglass figure has a narrow waist between fuller bust and hips.

clue.text: Sister church hiding where money's saved — source of trouble?

indicators.note: hiding says the sister and church pieces enclose the savings account

parts.note: a nun is a religious sister
an ISA is a British Individual Savings Account
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A nun at church hides the parish savings, causing problems.
explanation.walkthrough: An ISA is a UK tax-free savings account; 'hiding' tucks it inside the sister, with the church after.
explanation.definitionFit: A pest or irritation is something that causes annoyance and bother.

clue.text: New stain besetting leading supporter of disorder

indicators.note: besetting means surrounding, so the jumbled letters close round the other piece
new signals that the letters of stain take a fresh order

parts.note: arch means chief or leading, as in arch-enemy

explanation.surface: A fresh mark surrounds a prominent champion of chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' signals the anagram of stain, and 'besetting' wraps those letters round the word for leading, as in arch-rival.
explanation.definitionFit: An anarchist advocates abolishing government, so they favour lawlessness.

clue.text: Normal maritime passage in broadcast

indicators.note: in broadcast says the word is to be heard spoken

parts.note: a strait is a narrow sea channel

explanation.surface: An ordinary sea route described on the radio.
explanation.definitionFit: Straight is slang for conventional or ordinary.

clue.text: Something discharged at home in news report

parts.note: a bullet is what a gun fires
in means at home

explanation.surface: A gunshot at a house makes the evening news.
explanation.definitionFit: A bulletin is a short official announcement of news.

clue.text: Supporter trapped by tall youth

indicators.note: trapped by says the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A friend has been cornered by a lanky teenager.
explanation.definitionFit: An ally is someone who backs or sides with you.

clue.text: Irregular matter (and ominous partly)

indicators.note: partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An odd affair, and a slightly threatening one.
explanation.definitionFit: Something random follows no pattern or regular order.

clue.text: A lawyer holding the latest plan for meeting

indicators.note: holding says the first pieces close round the information

parts.note: a DA is an American district attorney
gen is slang for the latest information

explanation.surface: A lawyer has the newest proposal for a gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' slots the latest information between the article and the American lawyer, rather than inside the lawyer alone.
explanation.definitionFit: An agenda lists the items to be discussed at a gathering.

clue.text: Bring up sister?

explanation.surface: Raise your sibling?
explanation.walkthrough: In British hospitals a sister is a senior ward nurse.
explanation.definitionFit: To nurse a child is to rear it; a sister is a senior hospital carer in Britain.

clue.text: An arty view in the main?

definitions.text: An arty view in the main?

parts.words: An arty view in the main?
parts.note: reads as an artistic opinion in general, but 'the main' is the sea, so it means a painting of the ocean

explanation.definitionFit: It is a picture depicting the ocean, a marine landscape painting.

clue.text: Very severe writer, a lecturer

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: A harsh author who also teaches at university.
explanation.definitionFit: Penal terms or rates are punishingly harsh.

clue.text: Reportedly trim couple

indicators.note: reportedly says the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: to pare is to trim or cut back

explanation.surface: A neat-looking couple, so they say.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair is two of something together.

clue.text: Discordant organ in pad? Not this instrument!

indicators.note: discordant means jarring, so the letters of organ in pad are jumbled

explanation.surface: An out-of-tune organ in a flat would never be a concert grand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discordant' rearranges ORGAN IN PAD; the playful 'Not this' says the organ is not the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A grand piano is a large keyboard with horizontal strings.

clue.text: A singular political body banning a Democrat? It's given nod

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular

indicators.note: banning says a letter is excluded from the political body

parts.note: a senate is a legislative assembly
D stands for Democrat in US politics

explanation.surface: A single legislature voting out a Democrat agrees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banning' removes A from SENATE, leaving SENTE.
explanation.definitionFit: To be nodded through is to be agreed to, so it was approved.

clue.text: Copper, we hear, showing nerve

indicators.note: we hear says the word is spoken aloud

parts.note: copper is a metal

explanation.surface: A police officer, it's said, showing courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a police officer but is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Mettle is courage and spirit in facing difficulty.
